subject: Follow-up: RAG eval plan & retrieval/reranker options for Litera Health
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: discovery w/ Litera — primary asks and quick quals

Team — quick notes from today's discovery with Kenji and Dr. Moreno at Litera Health (30m):

Summary of need:
- They want an in-product RAG experience over clinical support docs and internal SOPs for care coordinators. Goal: accurate anchored answers with per-response source links (doctor-reviewed) and <300ms median generation latency for short queries.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + BM25 for retrieval; they see frequent ungrounded answers when using their current LLM experiments and worry about hallucinations (particularly for medication dosing guidance).
- Data residency: US-only. HIPAA concern; they asked about on-prem / Private option for PHI-sensitive subsets.

Key constraints:
- Latency target: median end-to-end <300ms for typical 1-2 sentence answers.
- Cost: evaluating mid-range models first (no immediate appetite for 70B+ always-on unless we can show clear perf/cost tradeoffs).
- SLA: eventually will want a 99.9% uptime for production clinical path.

Immediate asks from Litera:
- Recommended model candidates for RAG (small/medium vs canonical): tradeoffs and cost estimates
- Baseline benchmark for recall@5, grounding rate (source attribution %), and hallucination rate on a 250-query prompt set
- Suggested retrieval settings (chunking, overlap, index + vector config) and a reranker recommendation
- A short mutual action plan + timeline to run a targeted eval using a sanitized sample (they can provide ~500 doc excerpts)

My initial recommendations (for discussion before we send):
1) Models to eval: Redwood-search-3b (fast, low-cost), Llama-3-13B-chat-compat (balanced quality), and a quantized 33B candidate if we need more factuality. Call out estimated token costs in the doc.
2) Retrieval: keep BM25 prefiltering (their infra) + FAISS HNSW vector index for semantic re-rank. Chunk size 150-300 tokens with 40-50 token overlap appears appropriate for their clinical docs.
3) Reranker: test both a lightweight cross-encoder (monoT5-like reranker) and a hybrid re-ranker tuned for medical entity overlap. Measure top-1 grounding precision and top-5 recall.
4) Grounding metrics: measure Top-k grounding rate (percentage of answers with at least one source cited among top-k retrieved), R-precision, and a hallucination audit (human labeler verifies factual claims vs sources).

Attachments: raggap_config.yaml (config stub), litera_eval_promptset_v1.jsonl (250 sample queries), evaluation_summary.csv (placeholder for results).

Next steps proposed to Kenji (draft): ask for sanitized sample of 250–500 docs, permission to ingest into a temporary eval index (US-only), and agreement on 2 retrieval + 2 reranker configs to run in parallel.

I will draft the external note. Thoughts on model candidates or anything to add?

—Sergio

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Kenji Saito <kenji.saito@litera.health>, Dr. Lucia Moreno <lucia.moreno@litera.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery w/ Litera — primary asks and quick quals

Kenji / Dr. Moreno — thanks, good questions. Below are concrete answers and a proposed short eval plan.

1) Prompt templates / scoring approach:
- We typically run a short system prompt that: 1) instructs the model to answer concisely, 2) require a source citation for each factual claim, and 3) include a fallback "I don't know — please consult source" if the model cannot find supporting text.
- Example prompt (sent as single message):
  "You are a clinical knowledge assistant. Based on the documents retrieved, answer the user query. Provide a single concise answer (1-3 sentences) and list the document titles and offsets you used as sources. If you cannot find a supported answer, respond: 'Insufficient information in the provided documents.'"
- Scoring grounding: automated check that each claim token spans text that exists in any of the top-k retrieved chunks (string match + normalized punctuation). Then human audit for hallucination rate (labels: Supported / Not supported / Needs human review).

2) US-only eval & PHI — yes. We can run the eval inside your private VPC via Redwood Private or via a dedicated ephemeral Private eval environment. We will not persist raw PHI; we only index sanitized excerpts you approve. We can also run with customer-managed KMS. I'll loop our security lead if you want an architecture diagram.

3) Quick benchmark (ballpark on our internal clinical test set):
- Redwood-search-3b + HNSW + monoT5-reranker: recall@5 ~ 0.78, median end-to-end latency (query → 3 candidate generations + reranker) ~ 210–320ms depending on sequence length; cost: low.
- Llama-3-13B-chat (quantized) + same stack: recall@5 ~ 0.82, median latency ~320–420ms; higher token cost but better fluency and slightly better grounding in our tests.
Notes: these numbers vary with chunk size and average doc length; we'll run your dataset to get concrete numbers.

Proposed eval matrix (2 weeks):
- Retrieval configs: (A) BM25 prefilter + FAISS HNSW vectors (chunk size 200, overlap 50) and (B) BM25 + FAISS with chunk size 350, overlap 75.
- Rerankers: (1) lightweight cross-encoder (monoT5 style) and (2) medically tuned cross-encoder (entity-aware).
- Models: Redwood-search-3b and Llama-3-13B-chat-quant.
- Metrics: recall@1/5, Top-k grounding rate, R-precision, median latency, and human-labeled hallucination rate on a 250-sample audit.

Deliverables: evaluation_summary.csv (automated metrics) + short slide deck with sample grounded vs ungrounded responses and recommended config.

Action items / timeline:
- Today: Kenji to confirm permission to ingest sanitized subset and drop a sample to the shared Drive link.
- +3 business days: Redwood to index sample and run first-pass automated metrics for both retrieval configs.
- +7 business days: Human audit of 250 queries and final recommendation.

Links: benchmark stub + promptset are here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3LiteraRAG-benchmark (we uploaded the sample promptset and a starter config).

If this looks good, we'll kick off once you drop the sanitized docs.

Thanks — Sergio
